text: {"summary":"Buying $5,000 of QQQ with new money would increase the portfolio’s total value from $15,001 to $20,001 and lower its cash share from 2.5% to 1.9%. The trade would also change the portfolio’s company and sector exposures and its replayed crash results.","points":["The listed shares of NVDA, AAPL, and AMZN would each be lower after the trade, while Technology would rise from 42.5% to 46.9%. Consumer cyclical would move from 19.7% to 17.3%, and Financial services from 8.1% to 6.1%.","In the crash replays, the worst percentage fall would change from 56.4% to 55.4% for the financial crisis, 30.7% to 30.0% for Covid, and 32.8% to 33.3% for 2022. The replayed dollar falls would be larger after the trade in all three cases.","In the 2008–09 crisis, the market fell 55.2% from peak to bottom; after the 2009-03-09 bottom, it gained 71.9% in one year and 114.3% in three years, and took 41.3 months to recover. Selling near that bottom would have meant missing some of the subsequent gains; buying near the preceding peak would have been followed by the decline.","In the Covid crash, the market fell 33.7% from peak to bottom; after the 2020-03-23 bottom, it gained 77.5% in one year and 84.6% in three years, and took 4.6 months to recover. Selling near that bottom would have meant missing some of the subsequent gains; buying near the preceding peak would have been followed by the decline."]}
